title: Add latency-affinity probe and traffic seam for phase-correlated canary detection
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: New affinity-based canary detector: groups traffic by request affinity and detects phase-correlated tail-latency regressions. Adds a traffic seam mechanism to safely pause or reduce canary weights when correlated regressions are detected.
description:
Motivation: existing canary detectors focus on population-level metrics (p50/p95) which miss phase-aligned regressions that only affect specific request clusters. This PR implements a latency-affinity probe and a traffic seam that (1) groups requests by lightweight affinity keys, (2) maintains EWMA-backed quantile sketches per affinity bucket, (3) computes a correlation score to identify phase-correlated increases in tail latency, and (4) ties this signal to the rollout guard to automatically throttle or pause canaries when correlated degradation is observed.

What this change contains (high-level):
- latency_affinity_probe: new probe module that extracts a 4-part affinity key (route, prompt-length-bin, recent-kv-hash-prefix, model-variant) and assigns traffic into buckets.
- affinity_quantiles: sketching + EWMA layer that maintains p50/p95/p99 over a 2m sliding horizon with half-life tuning to respond to short-lived spikes but ignore micro-noise.
- correlation_scoring: computes Spearman rank correlation and a weighted percentile divergence score across synchronous buckets to detect phase-alignment.
- traffic_seam_controller: rollout guard integration that clamps canary weight, puts the canary into "seamed" mode (traffic diverted to a shadowed pool), and emits reasons for operator visibility.
- dashboards/alerts: Grafana panels and Alertmanager rules for affinity churn, seam activation, and top offending affinity buckets.
- canary-simulator tests: synthetic workloads to validate sensitivity/precision trade-offs and false-positive rate at 0.6% target.

Checklist: 
- [x] Probe + controller implementation
- [x] Unit tests for affinity extraction and quantile sketches
- [x] Integration tests using canary-simulator (deterministic scenarios)
- [x] E2E smoke in staging with real traffic shadowing for 24h
- [x] Docs (guide + config reference)
- [x] Observability (metrics, traces, dashboards)

Performance and safety notes:
- The affinity key is intentionally compact (4 fields, hashed) to keep memory footprint low. In our staging run with 2M requests/day we observed ~12k active buckets and ~0.6% increase in runtime CPU during probe sampling.
- Default sensitivity is conservative: we require correlation_score >= 0.7 and sustained percentile delta (p95 delta > 35ms for 3 consecutive 10s windows) before the seam triggers. These thresholds are configurable per-service.

Why it's different from previous detectors:
- This detector specifically targets phase-correlated regressions (e.g., specific prompt templates, transient upstream service outages that affect a subset of requests, or cache warmup patterns) that do not materially change aggregate p95 immediately.
- Instead of only comparing canary vs baseline aggregates, we look for synchronous divergence across affinity buckets to reduce false positives driven by traffic composition shifts.

Testing summary: 
- Unit: 45 tests added, coverage +3.2% for probe package.
- Integration: canary-simulator scenarios included: 'phase_spike', 'mixed_payload_regression', 'noisy_background' — the detector correctly identified phase_spike and remained silent on noisy_background.
- Staging: deployed with canary weight 5% on redwood-service-beta for 24h, seam remained idle; synthetic phase spike injected at hour 3 activated seam and rollback path as expected.

Migration and config:
- Feature gated behind perf.affinity_probe.enabled=false by default; rollout plan: enable in staging for 2 weeks, tune thresholds, enable in production for low-traffic services first.

Related work and docs: linear/ENG-7123 contains the design doc and decision log. Short guide added to docs/canaries/affinity-probe.md and sample config in examples/canary-configs/affinity.yaml.
